relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Memory begins with Adam, Seth, and Enosh.
Kenan, Mahalalel, and Jared carry the remembered line.
Enoch, Methuselah, and Lamech are named.
Noah's household opens into Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Japheth's descendants spread through many peoples and shores.
Gomer's line is remembered through Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's line moves toward islands, ports, and distant coasts.
Ham's descendants include Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush's household branches toward Seba, Havilah, Raamah, Sheba, and Dedan.
Nimrod is remembered as an early figure of earthly might.
Mizraim's descendants become communities with their own names.
The list remembers peoples connected with Egypt and Philistine origins.
Canaan's line begins with Sidon and Heth.
Jebusite, Amorite, and Girgashite communities enter the archive.
Hivite, Arkite, and Sinite communities are named.
Arvadite, Zemarite, and Hamathite peoples remain in memory.
Shem's descendants connect Israel's story with Elam, Asshur, Aram, and others.
Arpachshad, Shelah, and Eber continue the line.
Peleg and Joktan are remembered at a time of division.
Joktan's household begins to unfold.
Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah remain named.
Ebal, Abimael, and Sheba remain named.
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab complete Joktan's remembered sons.
The line narrows again: Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah.
Eber, Peleg, and Reu carry the memory forward.
Serug, Nahor, and Terah approach Abraham's generation.
Abram is remembered by the transformed name Abraham.
Isaac and Ishmael both remain within Abraham's family record.
Ishmael's line begins with Nebaioth and continues through named sons.
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema are remembered.
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah complete Ishmael's named sons.
Keturah and her descendants widen Abraham's remembered household.
Midian's descendants preserve another branch of Keturah's line.
Isaac's sons, Esau and Israel, stand beside one another in memory.
Esau's descendants are named without erasure.
Eliphaz's household includes Timna and Amalek within ancient memory.
Reuel's sons are remembered.
Seir's descendants preserve the indigenous memory of Edom's land.
Timna is named as Lotan's sister, interrupting a male-only archive.
The houses of Shobal and Zibeon continue.
Anah and Dishon lead into another remembered household.
Ezer and Dishan's descendants close Seir's family list.
Edom's kings are remembered before Israel possesses a monarchy.
Bela dies and Jobab succeeds him.
Jobab dies and Husham succeeds him.
Husham dies and Hadad succeeds through a history already marked by war.
Hadad dies and Samlah succeeds him.
Samlah dies and Shaul succeeds him.
Shaul dies and Baal-hanan succeeds him.
Hadad's reign remembers his city and the women Mehetabel, Matred, and Me-zahab.
Edom's political memory shifts from kings to chiefs.
Oholibamah, Elah, and Pinon are named among the chiefs.
Kenaz, Teman, and Mibzar are named among the chiefs.
Magdiel and Iram close the remembered chiefs of Edom.

contemplative_note: The first chapter refuses the fantasy that sacred history belongs to one isolated bloodline. It remembers neighboring peoples, women, rival houses, and Edomite rulers before Israel's monarchy. Genealogy can become belonging only when it refuses blood purity, inherited blame, and the erasure of those outside the narrator's center.
